title: The Speaker's Chair

endcard.line: Pictures: David Castor (public domain); unknown photographer (public domain)

segments.say: Every sitting of the Lok Sabha is run from one chair. Who sits in it, and how much power does it hold?

anim.title: Choosing the Speaker
items: Article 93: the House chooses its Speaker
Stays on after dissolution until the new House meets

segments.say: Under Article ninety-three, the Lok Sabha chooses its Speaker from its own members. If the House is dissolved, the Speaker stays on until the new House meets.

right.title: Speaker
items: no vote in the first instance
a casting vote in a tie

segments.say: The Speaker does not vote in the first instance. But if the votes are equal, the Speaker has a casting vote, under Article one hundred.
Two decisions carry special weight. The Speaker decides whether a bill is a Money Bill, and that decision is final.

anim.title: The anti-defection law
items: Is a member disqualified for defection?

segments.say: Under the Tenth Schedule, the Speaker also decides whether a member is disqualified for defection.

anim.title: Removing a Speaker
items: Passed by a majority of all the then members
The Speaker does not preside meanwhile

segments.say: Removal needs fourteen days' notice and a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members. During that debate, the Speaker does not preside.
For GS Two, link the Speaker to Article ninety-three, the casting vote, Money Bills and the anti-defection law.

sources: Constitution of India, official English text (Legislative Department diglot PDF, legislative.gov.in, 'as on' 2024 edition): Art. 93 (House chooses Speaker and Deputy Speaker); Art. 94 (removal by resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, at least 14 days' notice; Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution until immediately before the first meeting of the new House); Art. 96 (not to preside while a removal resolution is under consideration); Art. 100(1) (no vote in the first instance, casting vote on equality of votes); Art. 110(3) (Speaker's decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final); Tenth Schedule para 6 (Speaker decides questions of disqualification on ground of defection)

quiz.q: When can the Speaker of the Lok Sabha vote on a question?
options: Only when the votes are equal
quiz.why: Art. 100(1): no vote in the first instance; a casting vote in a tie.

quiz.q: How much notice is needed to move a resolution to remove the Speaker?
quiz.why: Art. 94: at least fourteen days' notice.

quiz.q: Who decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
quiz.why: Art. 110(3): the Speaker's decision is final.

reviewNote: All facts are from the official Constitution text. The script does not repeat Tenth Schedule paragraph 7 (the bar on courts), because courts have reviewed Speakers' decisions since; don't add it. The 1950 Assembly photo shows a crowd of members, all historical. Moving facts: none.
